A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ChainMPQ work and are readable throughout, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained, relocated, and newly added material can be reliably distinguished.

before.justification: V1 reports original MMRel and R-Bench experiments, component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity results, and qualitative attention analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds model comparisons, latency experiments, MMBench/MME evaluations, and another case study.

M1.justification: The main five-question design is retained. Section 4.3 adds two lightweight inference variants: Light1 runs Q1/Q2 in parallel and passes their answers and attention masks to Q5; Light2 retains Q3–Q5. These are limited procedural adaptations.

E1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds actual evaluations on MMBench and MME, extending coverage beyond relational yes/no judgments to broader perception and reasoning tasks, including recognition, OCR, numerical reasoning, and translation. MMRel and R-Bench remain. The additional comparative case belongs to already covered MMRel relations.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds standard Chain-of-Thought prompting as an evaluated comparator, including for the original two models. Vanilla inference, Constraint-Aware Prompting, and Detect-then-Calibrate remain. Triplet Description is newly discussed but is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The main evaluation adds Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3.5-8B configurations. New experiments introduce per-sample latency, accuracy gain per additional second, and aggregate MMBench/MME metrics. R-Bench's image-level setting is clarified rather than demonstrably changed. Appendix Tables 3–4 label their InternVL model 'InternVL3-8B,' leaving its correspondence to the main-text configuration unclear.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds an accuracy–latency analysis of full ChainMPQ versus Light1/Light2. Appendix A.6.2 and Figure 7 add a light-versus-mirror size-comparison case. The original component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, and action/spatial attention cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's improvement columns report score differences, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: All original Table 1 scores and Figure 3 ablation/sensitivity results are retained. V2 adds CoT and newer-model results, latency measurements, MMBench/MME scores, and a comparative-case outcome. For example, Table 2 reports MMRel accuracy/latency of 63.78%/1.5 seconds for Light1 versus 65.20%/3.3 seconds for full ChainMPQ; these are new variant comparisons, not version-to-version gains.

T1.justification: Equation (2) corrects the attention-aggregation denominator from |T|K to |T|n, matching the sum over n decoder layers. This resolves a mismatched normalization symbol. The remaining mathematical formulation is substantively retained, and neither version introduces theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free relational reasoning through question decomposition and accumulated textual/visual memory reduces relation hallucinations. Mentioning four evaluated models expands the supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new general-benchmark results as evidence that better relational understanding supports broader reasoning, recommends Light1 when balancing accuracy and latency, and uses the comparative case to argue wider applicability. The existing limitations concerning attention as a proxy and visual-token granularity remain.

D1.justification: V2 discloses GPT-3.5 Turbo question refinement, R-Bench's image-level setup, Prompt 10 for Constraint-Aware Prompting, and unchanged released parameters for Detect-then-Calibrate. It clarifies ablation context handling and adds a project-page pointer. V1's writing-only LLM-use statement and two-A6000/throughput disclosure are removed. The PDFs do not establish when GPT refinement entered the implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of Triplet Description/Tri-HE and citations for the newly evaluated models and benchmarks. Its positioning relative to ICoT and relational-hallucination research remains substantially unchanged. The additional dated CoT reference represents an already cited work.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and most existing prose remain. V2 makes localized rewrites, standardizes the acronym expansion, inserts a performance section, and expands/reorganizes appendix subsections. Author affiliations and publication headers change, acknowledgments are added, and the LLM-usage subsection is removed.

P2.justification: The displayed evidence expands substantially: Table 1 gains CoT rows and two model blocks, Tables 2–4 are added, and Figure 7 introduces another illustrated case. Existing figures are relocated, while Figures 1–2 receive label and diagram corrections. The original ablation plot and attention visualizations remain.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evaluation of cross-model generality and practical usefulness through newer backbones, a relevant CoT control, and explicit accuracy–latency comparisons, addressing important gaps in v1. Additional implementation disclosures also improve assessability. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses: hardware information is removed, broader-task procedures remain underspecified, and Table 4 reports an InstructBLIP MME gain of 87.2 although its displayed scores imply 93.2.
